title: Robust and generalizable CNV detection for single-cell sequencing assays.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed every file in the RIDDLER GitHub repository (30 files, largest 3.4 MB) and downloaded three: data/SNU601_1MB.bed, features/features.1MB.csv and README.md. The .bed is a read-count table of 3,102 one-megabase genome windows (rows) x 100 cell barcodes (columns) plus 4 location columns, 10,846,256 total reads, 6.8% zeros, per-cell totals 50,097-440,027. features.1MB.csv has exactly 2 columns, GC (guanine-cytosine) fraction and mappability, 3,102 rows, no missing values. I also pulled the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) supplementary file lists for GSE97693 and GSE154873: GSE97693_RAW.tar is 770 GB and per-cell methylation files are ~1 GB each; GSE154873 holds gene-expression count matrices (~20 MB each), not copy-number calls. No copy-number label table exists in the repository or in either GEO series. Zenodo record 17259577 timed out twice (handshake timeout) and is recorded as unretrievable; the repository it archives is the same code.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the benchmark ground truth was produced by running AneuFinder on single-cell whole-genome sequencing of SNU601 from a separate experiment (SRA PRJNA498809), that ATAC-derived clusters were matched to whole-genome-sequencing subclones by consensus profile, and the reported subclone-recovery numbers (RIDDLER 6 of 7, Copy-scAT 4, epiAneufinder 3). I did not download any raw sequencing data; project rules forbid it.

a1_downloadable.note: Code, GC/mappability features and a 100-cell example count matrix download without login (verified). All underlying datasets are public (SRA, ENCODE, GEO, NeMO), no access application. Zenodo mirror timed out but is redundant with GitHub.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. No copy-number state is a column anywhere. To get labels you must align raw single-cell whole-genome sequencing reads (PRJNA498809), run AneuFinder, cluster cells into subclones, then match ATAC clusters to whole-genome subclones by consensus profile. That is label construction by inference across sources, exactly the A2 fail condition. Verified by listing the repository and both GEO series: only read counts and GC/mappability covariates are deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present in principle: the example file holds raw binned read counts and the feature files hold GC and mappability per window. But only 100 of the paper's cells are deposited; the rest require re-binning raw fragment files.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are unambiguous and verified: integer de-duplicated read counts per 1-megabase window per cell; GC as a fraction 0-0.66, mappability as a fraction 0-0.99.

a5_enough_rows.note: The deposited example alone gives 3,102 windows x 100 cells = 310,200 count cells, and the paper's full datasets have thousands of cells. Row count is not the problem here; labels are.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1 MB for the deposited example; 770 GB for GSE97693_RAW.tar, plus raw SRA runs needing alignment for the only labelled benchmark
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL for the real task. Binned matrices are tiny, but producing them (and the labels) means aligning raw single-cell whole-genome and ATAC sequencing. Verified file sizes in the GEO file lists.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing contradicts the paper: the repository file is explicitly a 100-cell demonstration subset, consistent with the README, and the paper's per-dataset cell counts are not reproducible from deposited files either way.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL, and this is the deeper failure. The 'ground truth' copy-number state is AneuFinder's output (another algorithm's prediction) computed from read depth, i.e. from the same class of feature the new model would use. Worse, the ATAC cells and the whole-genome cells are different cells from separate experiments, so labels are assigned at subclone-consensus level, not per cell. Stated in the paper's results text, which I read.

existing_models.name: RIDDLER (this paper; robust Poisson regression on read counts with GC, mappability and tissue-accessibility covariates)
existing_models.score_and_split: Recovered 6 of 7 single-cell whole-genome-sequencing subclones of the SNU601 gastric cancer line versus Copy-scAT 4 and epiAneufinder 3; copy-number match rate >=80% per clone. Evaluated on three-state (gain/loss/normal) calls against AneuFinder consensus subclone profiles, not a held-out split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cross-assay ground truth: ATAC and whole-genome experiments were performed separately on the same cell line, so cells cannot be paired and evaluation is limited to three states because the competing method epiAneufinder supports no more.

existing_models.name: epiAneufinder (Nature Communications 2023, R package)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published as a breakpoint-and-somy caller for single-cell ATAC-seq; in this paper's comparison it recovered 3 of 7 SNU601 subclones.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Does not model cell-type accessibility landscape, which this paper names as the largest bias source in ATAC coverage.

existing_models.name: Copy-scAT (R package, aggregates bins to chromosome-arm level)
existing_models.score_and_split: Recovered 4 of 7 SNU601 subclones in this paper's comparison.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Arm-level aggregation limits resolution; not stated by me from their own discussion.

existing_models.name: AtaCNA / AtaCNV (Cell Reports Methods 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as accurately detecting both large- and small-scale copy-number alterations from single-cell chromatin data; split and numbers not retrieved by me.

existing_models.name: CopyVAE (Bioinformatics 2024, variational autoencoder)
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report higher sensitivity and specificity than existing methods for copy-number inference from single-cell RNA sequencing (a different modality).

existing_models.name: Benchmarking studies: 'Benchmarking scRNA-seq copy number variation callers' (Nature Communications 2025) and 'Benchmarking copy number aberrations inference tools using single-cell multi-omics datasets' (Briefings in Bioinformatics 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Independent benchmarks of this exact task already published; I retrieved their titles and venues only.

backbone.name: scBasset or scGPT could embed single-cell ATAC profiles, but neither predicts copy number and neither helps without labels
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for the 1-MB binned matrices; irrelevant given no labels
backbone.licence: Not checked, as the project fails earlier

integration.partner_dataset: ENCODE K562 single-cell ATAC (ENCSR308ZGJ) and the DNase hypersensitivity index (Zenodo 3838751) are joinable on hg38 genomic coordinates
integration.join_key: hg38 genomic window coordinates (chr/start/end), present in the deposited .bed
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could ask whether accessibility-atlas covariates explain enough coverage bias to make copy-number calls transfer across assays, but with no per-cell truth labels the question cannot be answered quantitatively.

controls.positive_control: Known large gains and losses in SNU601 and the near-triploid K562 karyotype are textbook signals a working caller must recover; both would be usable if labels existed.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable in principle, but there are no labels to shuffle.
controls.external_validation: K562 single-cell ATAC (ENCODE) and long-read scNanoATAC (GSM5825633) would be genuine second sources, again only if someone first produced per-cell copy-number truth.

honest_claim_h3: At best: 'a supervised model trained on binned read counts plus GC, mappability and accessibility covariates reproduces AneuFinder's subclone-consensus copy-number calls for single-cell ATAC data from the same two cancer cell lines' — which is distilling an existing algorithm's output on two cell lines, not measuring copy number.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell chromatin read counts and genome bias features to predict each cell's copy number state per genomic window.
plain_idea.train_on: For each cell and each 1-megabase genome window: the de-duplicated read count plus that window's GC (guanine-cytosine) fraction, mappability and tissue-accessibility coverage. Verified 3,102 windows x 100 cells in the one deposited example; the paper's full cohorts are thousands of cells across two cancer cell lines, a healthy blood sample and brain tissue.
plain_idea.predict: The copy number state of that window in that cell (loss, normal, gain). The only available 'true answer' is AneuFinder's call on single-cell whole-genome sequencing of the same cell line run as a separate experiment, matched to ATAC cells at the subclone level, not cell to cell.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer biologists reading chromatin accessibility want to know which cells carry which amplifications without a second sequencing assay; a supervised caller could in principle beat hand-built statistical models. In practice the field already has four open callers and no per-cell truth labels to train against.

more_or_better_data.why: The deposited data is a 100-cell demonstration subset; everything else is raw sequencing already used by the four existing callers (epiAneufinder, Copy-scAT, AtaCNA, RIDDLER). We would have strictly less data than the paper itself.

confidence_score.why: RIDDLER already emits a per-window p-value for deviation from expectation (verified in the README's copy_call documentation), so per-prediction confidence is not a gap we could fill.

models_beatable.why: RIDDLER is a 2026 method that already beat the 2023 epiAneufinder and Copy-scAT on the same cell line, its R code is open on GitHub, and two independent 2025 benchmarks of this task exist. Nothing here is old or weak.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The condition that fails first is the evaluation split: there is no per-cell labelled set to split, because the only truth comes from different cells in a different assay, matched by consensus profile.

ml_idea: Considered: a supervised per-cell, per-window copy-number classifier for single-cell ATAC and single-cell methylation data, trained on read counts plus GC, mappability and accessibility covariates, with cell lines held out. It fails because the label is not deposited, must be reconstructed by aligning raw whole-genome sequencing and running AneuFinder, and is itself an algorithm's output derived from read depth.

effort.compute_note: The 1-megabase binned matrix I loaded used well under 1 GB of RAM, so modelling would be trivial on a laptop. The 770 GB figure is the GSE97693 raw archive size read from the GEO file list; building labels also needs read alignment of SRA runs, which I estimated at tens of hours and did not attempt.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the repository and the GEO supplementary files and ask 'is there a copy-number call table anywhere?'. Answer: no — 30 files, the only data file is a 100-cell count matrix. Two minutes, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A8. No copy-number label is deposited: it must be rebuilt by aligning raw whole-genome sequencing and running AneuFinder, and that label is another algorithm's output computed from read depth in a different experiment whose cells cannot be paired with the ATAC cells. Only a 100-cell demonstration matrix is downloadable (verified), while the labelled benchmark needs ~770 GB plus alignment (A6). The field also holds four open callers and two 2025 benchmarks, so even a successful model would be distilling RIDDLER on two cell lines.
